ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #9
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. Only one word repeated
   C. No full stops
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

2. When practising Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot.

3. When practising Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.

4. When practising Play: Structure and Setting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Play: Structure and Setting.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Play: Structure and Setting.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Play: Structure and Setting.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Play: Structure and Setting.

5. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.

6. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.

7. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.

8. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.

9. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the Library
   B. Where is the library
   C. where is the library
   D. Where is the library?

10. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. Only an action
   C. A person, place, thing, or idea
   D. Only a describing word

11. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. run
   B. happiness
   C. blue
   D. quickly

12. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in use 15.3.1 Sentences- 15.3.1.1 Imperative – commands, requests 15.3.1 and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 15.4.1 Intensive reading: Poems and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — One main idea with supporting sentences

2. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot.

3. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.

4. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Play: Structure and Setting.

5. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.

6. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.

7. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.

8. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.

9. D — Where is the library?

10. C — A person, place, thing, or idea

11. A — run

12. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in use 15.3.1 Sentences- 15.3.1.1 Imperative – commands, requests 15.3.1; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 15.4.1 Intensive reading: Poems; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
